To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) bone changes following total knee arthoplasty are characterized by a phase of accelerated bone resorption followed by partial recovery; (ii) bone changes are more pronounced in the LL projection, particularly in the distal femoral region; (iii) the greatest bone loss is observed in the first 2 months from surgery; (iv) bone changes in the AP projection are fully recovered within one year from surgery while the LL projection shows residual bone loss at the end of the observation period
the pattern of bone changes after total arthroplasty of the knee follows the well known design: an initial accelerated bone loss followed by a phase of partial bone recover.
bone loss after knee surgery is not a simple process, and that bone loss after surgery is not a linear process, but a process with a complex time course.
